title: Customer-facing debugging flow for LLM output variance
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes a reproducible, customer-facing debugging and escalation flow for investigating reports of inconsistent or degraded LLM outputs (quality variance, hallucinations, or surprising style/length changes). It is written for Customer Success (CS) engineers and first-line support, and includes data collection templates, quick mitigations, metric thresholds, synthetic test guidance, and an escalation matrix for SRE/Model teams.

When to use:
- Customer reports that previously-stable prompts now return lower-quality or inconsistent answers.
- Widespread deviations observed after a deploy, model switch, or config change.
- Intermittent variance tied to time-of-day, tenant load, or routing changes.

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Confirm customer-visible failure with a single canonical example. Ask customer to provide: a reproducible prompt, desired behavior, timestamp (UTC), and the request-ID if available.
2) Check service health dashboard (Redwood Console) for model rollout events, latency spikes, or capacity fallback during the incident window.
3) Lock sampling settings: ask customer to run with explicit parameters (model, model_version, temperature, top_p, max_tokens) and collect both request and response payloads.
4) If output is inappropriate, offer immediate mitigation: set temperature=0.0-0.2, pin to last-known-good model_version, and enable deterministic sampling if supported.

Mandatory data collection (customer + CS):
- Canonical prompt(s) (1–5) that reproduce the issue.
- Full request payload including headers and query params.
- Full response payload(s) (including streaming chunks).
- Exact model name and model_version / build id.
- Sampling parameters: temperature, top_k/top_p, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, max_tokens, stop sequences.
- Date/time (UTC) and request-id(s).
- Customer SDK/SDK-version or API client and region.
- Any recent application changes (prompt templating, pre/post processing, tokenization or sanitization).

Triage flow (detailed steps):
1) Reproduce locally (CS):
   - Run the canonical prompt against the same model_version and sampling params. Use the customer’s SDK or our recommended curl to mirror environment.
   - Example curl (replace placeholders):
     curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
       -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>'
       -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
       -d '{"model":"<MODEL>","model_version":"<VERSION>","input":"<PROMPT>","temperature":0.2,"max_tokens":256}'
2) If not reproducible:
   - Query logs for the customer request-id and window.
   - Check for routing/fanout proxies, A/B rollout headers, tenant isolation, or fallback to quantized model variants.
   - Ask customer to run with explicit model_version pinned.
3) If reproducible and deterministic changes observed:
   - Compare outputs across three axes: exact token sequences (string diff), n-gram overlap, and semantic similarity (embedding cosine).
   - Compute a quick similarity score: run an embedding on both outputs and compare cosine similarity. Threshold guidance is below.
4) Investigate probable root causes by triage category:
   - Model rollout / version change: check deployment events, rollout percentage, and canary logs.
   - Sampling/config drift: verify client-sent params vs server defaults (auto-top-p overrides, max_tokens truncation).
   - Prompt pre/post-processing: templating errors, accidental whitespace/newline changes, or escaping errors.
   - KV cache or context clipping: long histories may evict critical context; verify total tokens and effective context window.
   - Quantization or runtime variant mismatch: customer's tenant routed to a quantized runtime variant may produce stylistic differences.
   - Non-deterministic ops under load: continuous batching and token-level latency management can alter timing-sensitive sampling; check concurrency and burst events.

Similarity thresholds (guidance table):
- Metric | Action threshold | Notes
- Embedding cosine similarity | < 0.82 => likely semantic regression -> escalate to Model team
- BLEU / ROUGE quick overlap | drop > 30% from baseline => quality regression on structured tasks
- Exact token match rate | < 60% on deterministic tasks => sampling/config mismatch

Synthetic validation (set up a short suite):
- Purpose: reproduce, quantify regression, and create a stable artifact for ML/evals.
- Minimal suite design: 10–50 golden prompts that exercise critical behavior (edge cases, api-specific formatting, regulated phrasing).
- Example run command (ci-friendly):
  - curl the test harness endpoint which runs the prompt set and returns JSON with metrics.
  - Sample harness response fields to capture: prompt_id, baseline_embedding, current_embedding, cosine_similarity, tokens_used, model_version.

Immediate mitigations to offer customers (ordered by risk):
1) Pin model_version to last-known-good. Notes: This is the fastest control but may require org permission for dedicated tenants.
2) Reduce temperature and randomness settings (temperature <= 0.2, top_p <= 0.6).
3) Shorten the effective context window (trim history) to avoid context clipping.
4) Route to an alternate runtime pool (non-quantized) if stylistic differences are suspected to come from quantization.
5) Temporarily enable a content filter or safety layer to block hallucinations while investigation proceeds.

Escalation matrix and SLAs:
- Level 1 (CS): initial triage, data collection, and mitigation offer. Target response time: 30 minutes SLA for P1 customer-impacting degradation. Owner: customer-success.
- Level 2 (SRE/runtime): investigate routing, runtime variant, capacity/fallback, and rollout telemetry. Target: 2 hours SLA for initial findings. Owner: eng-sre/eng-serving-runtime.
- Level 3 (Model/Applied ML): analyze model regressions, run eval harness, and propose model rollback or fine-tune. Target: 24–72 hours depending on severity. Owner: research/applied-ml.

Escalation template (to open an internal incident ticket):
- Title: [CS-INC] Output variance observed — tenant <TENANT_ID> — model <MODEL>@<VERSION>
- Required attachments: canonical prompts, customer request-ids, curl reproduction, synthetic harness results (if available), console timeline screenshot.
- Priority guidance: P1 if customer go-live affected or high-volume production impact.

Post-incident steps and ownership:
1) CS: confirm customer mitigation acceptance and document customer impact in ticket.
2) SRE: annotate deployment and routing events in incident ticket; capture logs and traces.
3) Model team: run regression evaluation, publish a short technical RCA and proposed actions (rollback, parameter change, or retrain).
4) Product/CS: schedule a customer-facing summary and QBR note if impact was material.
5) Create a regression test (golden prompts) and add to the continuous evaluation harness with a regression alert threshold.

Appendix A — Required CLI/API snippets:
- Fetch request details (example):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" "https://console.redwood.ai/v1/requests?request_id=<REQ_ID>"
- Run basic embed compare (pseudo):
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"embed-small","input":["OUTPUT_A","OUTPUT_B"]}'
